pronunciation.notes: Stress the An. The u is short, like the u in 'put'. In the plural, Ankünfte, it becomes ü: AHN-kuenf-tuh.

word.shortDefinition: The moment someone or something gets to where it was going.

intro.title: Let's start at the airport
paragraphs: You've just landed in Frankfurt after a twelve-hour flight. You're tired, you're looking for your bag, and you follow the big yellow signs. One of them says Ankunft. That's where you are: arrivals.
Ankunft is the German word for arrival. You'll see it on every airport sign, every train timetable and every hotel booking. You'll need it from your very first day in a German-speaking country.

etymology.title: Where it comes from

parts.note: The same an as in am Bahnhof (at the station).
An old noun made from kommen (to come). It survives only inside compound words.

etymology.summary: An arrival is the moment you come to a place.

bonus.note: Zu means toward. The future is whatever is coming toward you. Once you know -kunft, a whole group of words opens up: see the family below.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: the verb splits in two
keyTrap.explanation: The noun Ankunft stays in one piece, but its verb ankommen is a separable verb. In a normal sentence the an breaks off and moves to the very end. English speakers glue it back together all the time.

wrong.verdict: Not German. The an has to go to the end.

correct.german: Ich komme um acht Uhr an.
correct.literal: I come at eight o'clock at.
correct.note: The present tense: kommen in second place, an at the end.
The past tense: the ge slips in between, giving angekommen.

correct.german: Meine Ankunft ist um acht Uhr.
correct.literal: My arrival is at eight o'clock.
correct.note: Or skip the verb and use the noun. It never splits.

commonMistakes.title: The gender
commonMistakes.explanation: Ankunft is feminine. Here's a free rule: every noun ending in -kunft is feminine, so die Zukunft, die Herkunft and die Unterkunft too.

commonMistakes.title: The plural
commonMistakes.explanation: The plural adds -e and an umlaut. You'll see it on departure boards that list several trains at once.

commonMistakes.title: The linking s in compounds
commonMistakes.explanation: When Ankunft starts a longer word, German adds an s to join the parts. It's called the Fugen-s, and -kunft always takes it.

commonMistakes.title: The preposition after it
commonMistakes.explanation: You arrive in a city and at a place, so it's in or an, never nach. Nach is for travelling toward somewhere, not for getting there.

sampleSentences.german: Die Ankunft des Zuges verzögert sich um zehn Minuten.
sampleSentences.english: The train's arrival is delayed by ten minutes.

sampleSentences.german: Bei der Ankunft im Hotel bekommen Sie Ihren Schlüssel.
sampleSentences.english: You'll get your key when you arrive at the hotel.

sampleSentences.german: Wann kommst du in Hamburg an?
sampleSentences.english: When do you arrive in Hamburg?

sampleSentences.german: Schick mir bitte nach deiner Ankunft eine Nachricht.
sampleSentences.english: Please send me a message after you arrive.

sampleSentences.german: Auf der Anzeigetafel stehen alle Ankünfte und Abfahrten.
sampleSentences.english: The board shows all arrivals and departures.

sampleSentences.german: Es kommt darauf an, wie das Wetter wird.
sampleSentences.english: It depends on what the weather does. (Bonus phrase: ankommen auf means “to depend on.”)

quiz.prompt: Der Zug kommt um neun Uhr ___.
quiz.fullAnswer: Der Zug kommt um neun Uhr an.
quiz.explanation: Ankommen is separable, so an moves to the end of the sentence.
The plural adds -e and an umlaut. If your keyboard has no ü, write ue.

quiz.prompt: ___ Ankunft ist um acht Uhr. (der, die or das?)
quiz.fullAnswer: Die Ankunft ist um acht Uhr.
quiz.explanation: Every noun ending in -kunft is feminine.
When Ankunft starts a compound, it takes the linking s.

quiz.fullAnswer: Wann ist deine Ankunft in Berlin?
quiz.explanation: You arrive in a city, so it's in. Nach is for travelling toward a place.

memoryHook: An + kunft = a coming-to. When the train comes to the platform, that's die Ankunft. And the verb splits: Ich komme an.
